correctness.rationale: The general-m formula is mathematically correct. Distinct reciprocal lattices meet only at zero because 1,sqrt(p_2),...,sqrt(p_m) are rationally independent. Nonzero poles are simple and the residue coefficients follow directly. Quadratic-irrational Diophantine bounds give only polynomial coefficient growth for the chosen square-root family, ensuring tempered convergence. At zero, 1/Phi_m has parity m: when m is odd its principal part contains odd negative powers, whose boundary-value jump gives even delta derivatives through order m-1; when m is even the unit-mass symmetrization leaves the nonzero regular function 2(2i)^{-m}/Phi_m on every pole-free interval, so support is all of R. The weighted-simplex lattice count gives the stated R^m leading term. The m=3 specialization agrees with the exact coefficients and delta-double-prime term in the primary source.

originality.rationale: Originality fails under the required implication standard. The complete primary Tselishchev paper predates this record and, immediately after its m=3 theorem, explicitly states that the construction extends to any odd number of rationally independent frequencies with higher-order delta derivatives, while for an even number an analogous formula requires alternating signed masses instead of the unit counting measure. Its contour proof is exactly the reciprocal-sine boundary-value mechanism generalized by the audited package. The package adds explicit all-m coefficients, a full-support formulation for the even unit-mass case, and a counting asymptotic, but these are routine consequences/bookkeeping of an extension the source itself already announces and structurally explains; the headline odd/even dichotomy is therefore implication-covered.
